statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit. Consent UI prevented first-run interaction with underlying content, but server-rendered DOM, no-JS output, representative templates and objective browser evidence remained inspectable.

page.framework: Vue-like hydrated MPA (framework inferred from rendered comment markers; server-rendered content)
page.notes: m.bild.de redirects browser navigation to www.bild.de while retaining complete server-rendered news content. Representative coverage included homepage, section, article and search. Checkout, subscriber account management and deep video playback were not covered because they are distinct authenticated/commercial journeys and the first-run consent wall prevented entry.

paths.description: Entry page and news homepage; represents headline discovery, navigation, consent, responsive layout, privacy and performance.
Current sports story; represents article/detail pages, article metadata, media and no-JavaScript delivery.
Search landing page; represents the primary interactive find-content journey.

findings.summary: Consent-or-subscribe wall blocks all content on every tested route
findings.evidence: Mobile and desktop screenshots of the homepage, section, article and search all show the same full-viewport modal before any content can be used. The only immediate paths are accepting tracking, opening settings, or paying for BILD Pur.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep privacy choices available without covering the core article/listing surface. Use a compact, dismissible consent UI and preserve a clearly equivalent no-tracking route without requiring payment.

findings.summary: The site does not provide a user-preference-driven dark theme
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the site remains light; the platform probe found no prefers-color-scheme rules and computed color-scheme is light/normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light dark color-scheme at the root and map surfaces/text to adaptive tokens, using light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no View Transition treatment
findings.evidence: The CSS/platform probe found no view-transition usage across the homepage bundle, while the site exposes many route and carousel state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-document and cross-document navigation with the View Transitions API, while retaining reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long news pages do not expose scroll-state guidance
findings.evidence: The article is about 4,749 CSS px high and the homepage about 25,889 CSS px, but the CSS probe found no scroll timeline and screenshots show no reading-progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight CSS scroll-driven progress indicator and adapt sticky chrome using scroll-state/container queries where supported.

findings.summary: The primary read/search journeys are gated before they begin
findings.evidence: All four representative routes are obscured by the consent-or-pay wall; the agent could inspect server-rendered content but a first-time user cannot read or search before choosing tracking or subscription.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow the core news and search journeys to begin while presenting proportionate consent controls that do not replace the page.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured performance 0.53, FCP 8.7 s, LCP 16.3 s and TTI 16.5 s. A separate warm trace measured LCP 2.22 s, showing the cold path is the material risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce render-blocking CSS and startup JavaScript, and defer consent/advertising dependencies until needed.

findings.summary: The critical path ships excessive render-blocking and unused resources
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 155 requests and 1.75 MB transferred during the sampled load, including 78 scripts; Lighthouse reported 2.96 MiB total, about 930 ms render-blocking savings, 185 KiB unused JS and 40 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit critical CSS, split and conditionally load non-core scripts, improve cache lifetimes, use font-display, and ensure the LCP image is discoverable and prioritised.

findings.summary: Some links and frames have no accessible name
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name and frame-title. The DOM probe counted 143 links with no visible or fallback text and 184 controls without a detected name; the image primitive found 32 images without alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive element and iframe a programmatic name, and provide meaningful alt text or explicit empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: Homepage document structure and compact controls weaken keyboard/AT navigation
findings.evidence: The homepage has no H1 and begins its sampled hierarchy at H3. The probe also found many carousel buttons rendered only 4 CSS px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a logical H1-to-H2/H3 hierarchy, verify keyboard order and focus-visible styles, and make carousel controls operable at a practical target size.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console; its run also reported an out-of-bounds source-map mapping for html-load.com/loader.min.js.map.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate uncaught/runtime console errors and publish valid source maps for production scripts.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS but found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking policy, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy on the audited document.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options), Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The pre-consent page has a large tracking and third-party footprint
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 26 third-party origins and a known AppNexus origin. The HAR attributed 149 of 155 requests and 1.62 MB to origins other than m.bild.de (including related BILD hosts), and cookies were created before consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise pre-consent network activity, delay optional analytics/advertising until an affirmative choice, batch necessary telemetry, and enforce a strict third-party budget.

findings.summary: Cookie and defensive policy posture is weak
findings.evidence: Seven of eight observed cookies were flagged insecure; several analytics identifiers were SameSite=None and two persisted for 400 days. The response also lacked clickjacking, referrer and permissions policies.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on all HTTPS cookies, use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential, shorten analytics lifetimes, and configure browser-enforced policies.

findings.summary: The installable news experience has no active offline controller
findings.evidence: A valid manifest is linked and includes icons, theme and language metadata, but the runtime probe found no controlling service worker.
findings.suggestedFix: If installability is intended, register a service worker and provide an offline article/shell fallback; otherwise remove misleading app-install signals.

findings.evidence: The first-run modal gives a prominent free “Alle akzeptieren” action while the no-tracking route costs €3.99/month (€2.99 for subscribers); no equivalent free reject action is presented in the initial view.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer a comparably prominent reject/non-personalised choice, use neutral button hierarchy, and keep consent revocable without tying privacy to payment.

findings.summary: Media and code delivery exceed a proportionate first-view budget
findings.evidence: The image audit found six oversized images and Lighthouse estimated 146 KiB image savings. The load also shipped 2.96 MiB overall despite the first viewport being blocked by consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized responsive images, defer offscreen media, compress font/image assets and enforce page-weight budgets per template.

findings.summary: robots.txt contains a syntax issue reported by Lighthouse
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the robots-txt audit with one error, although manual inspection confirmed public crawling rules and four sitemap declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the invalid robots.txt directive while retaining the intended crawler and sitemap policy.
